statement: Under Regulation 2022/2554 Article 45, financial entities may exchange cyber threat information and intelligence (indicators of compromise, tactics, techniques and procedures, alerts, configuration tools) only where sharing aims to enhance digital operational resilience, occurs within trusted communities, and is implemented through arrangements protecting sensitive information, governed by rules of conduct respecting business confidentiality, GDPR and competition guidelines; arrangements define participation conditions and the role of public authorities, ICT providers and platforms, and entities notify competent authorities of joining or leaving.

name: Competent authorities by entity type
statement: Compliance with Regulation 2022/2554 is ensured by the sectoral competent authority designated under each entity type's own legal act (e.g. Directive 2013/36/EU authorities, or the ECB for significant credit institutions), without prejudice to the Oversight Framework for critical ICT third-party providers.

name: Cooperation with NIS2 structures
statement: ESAs and competent authorities may participate in the NIS2 Cooperation Group, consult CSIRTs and single points of contact, and request technical advice and set up fast-response coordination arrangements with NIS2 authorities, including coordinating investigations and inspections of entities that are both NIS2 essential or important entities and designated critical ICT providers.

name: Cooperation between authorities and cross-sector exercises
statement: Competent authorities, ESAs, the ECB and the Lead Overseer must cooperate closely and promptly exchange information on critical providers; the ESAs may establish practice-sharing mechanisms and cross-sector cyber crisis exercises to build coordinated Union-level response to systemic cross-border ICT incidents.

name: Supervisory powers and penalties
statement: Competent authorities must have all powers needed to enforce Regulation 2022/2554, including document access, on-site inspections, interviews, corrective measures, cease-and-desist orders, data traffic records, and public notices; Member States set effective, proportionate, dissuasive penalties applicable also to management body members, with reasoned decisions subject to appeal.

name: Penalty determination factors
statement: Under Regulation 2022/2554, competent authorities exercise penalty powers directly, in collaboration, by delegation or via judicial authorities, and set the type and level of penalty by weighing intent or negligence, materiality, gravity and duration, degree of responsibility, financial strength, profits gained or losses avoided, third-party losses, cooperation and previous breaches.

name: Publication of penalties
statement: Under Regulation 2022/2554, competent authorities publish final administrative penalty decisions with breach type, responsible persons and penalties, but may defer, anonymise or withhold publication where it would be disproportionate or jeopardise financial stability or a criminal investigation; appeals outcomes are added and publication lasts at most five years.

name: Criminal penalties option
statement: Member States may forgo administrative penalties for breaches subject to national criminal penalties, but must then ensure authorities can liaise with judicial authorities and share information on criminal proceedings with other competent authorities and the ESAs; Member States notify implementing laws by 17 January 2025.

name: Professional secrecy and data protection
statement: Confidential information under Regulation 2022/2554 is covered by professional secrecy binding all current and former authority personnel and delegates, disclosable only under Union or national law; ESAs and authorities may process personal data only as necessary and under GDPR or Regulation 2018/1725, retaining it at most 15 years.

name: Delegated powers and review clauses
statement: Regulation 2022/2554 confers delegated powers on the Commission for five years (tacitly renewable, revocable, subject to Parliament and Council objection), and requires Commission reviews of critical provider designation, third-country regime, JON, payment systems scope and statutory auditors.

name: Sectoral acts defer ICT rules to the Regulation
statement: Regulation 2022/2554 amends the sectoral acts for credit rating agencies, CCPs, trade repositories, CSDs, data reporting services (APAs, CTPs, ARMs) and critical benchmark administrators so that each must manage ICT systems, business continuity and recovery in accordance with Regulation 2022/2554, while ESMA technical standards under those acts exclude ICT risk and the duplicated provisions are deleted.

name: Entry into force and application date
statement: Regulation 2022/2554 entered into force on the twentieth day after publication in the Official Journal and applies from 17 January 2025.
